claims.harm: adding server-side aggregation options increases interface and code complexity and binds the project to backward-compatibility guarantees for formatting users can easily perform client-side
claims.quote: I quite strongly opppose the aggregation option, just a simple `bitcoin-cli getnetmsgstats` provides a user all the info they need. Visualization/aggregation can easily be done by the user, e.g. using `jq` or any other tool / aggregation they like, so adding that to our interface unnecessarily locks us into backwards compatibility promises and code/interface complexity
claims.settled_by_quote: I have now dropped the aggregation, which means removing commit d5a1ad981b `rpc: make it possible to aggregate the result in getnetmsgstats` and omitting the parts of the test that tested the aggregation

support.reason: Useful netstats for tracking. Normally, I'd sum and aggregate peer stats. This approach simplifies that.
lgtm. Tested on master and with v30.1 in my node monitoring dashboard.
Seems like useful info to expose. Approach-wise, I like that it adds very little logic in the RPC layer.

result.notes: First read of the discussion. stickies-v raised an objection against including RPC aggregation functionality, which vasild resolved by removing the aggregation commit and arguments.
